```{r}

# ============================================================
# TECHNICAL PRICING - 2027 AND 2028
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)

source("util.R")

# 1. LOAD CLEANED DATA --------------------------------------

book26 <- read.csv("data/book26.csv")
book27 <- read.csv("data/renewal_book_2027.csv")
book28 <- read.csv("data/renewal_book_2028.csv")

book26 <- set_types(book26)
book27 <- set_types(book27)
book28 <- set_types(book28)

# Ensure excess is categorical.
# Use consistent levels for all factor variables.

book26$ExcessChosen <- factor(book26$ExcessChosen)

factor_vars <- c(
  "VehicleType", "RiskZone", "AnnualKms",
  "GaragingLocation", "VehicleUse",
  "PaymentFrequency", "MultiPolicyFlag",
  "ExcessChosen"
)

for (v in factor_vars) {
  book26[[v]] <- factor(book26[[v]])
  book27[[v]] <- factor(
    book27[[v]], levels = levels(book26[[v]])
  )
  book28[[v]] <- factor(
    book28[[v]], levels = levels(book26[[v]])
  )
}

# Centre calendar year at 2026.
# This makes trend coefficients easier to interpret.

book26$YearTrend <- book26$Year - 2026
book26$Exposure <- as.numeric(book26$Exposure)

# Check required variables are complete.

predictors <- c(
  "DriverAge", "YearsLicensed", "VehAge",
  "VehValue", "VehicleType", "RiskZone",
  "Density", "AnnualKms", "ExcessChosen",
  "GaragingLocation", "VehicleUse",
  "NCDLevel", "TenureYears",
  "MultiPolicyFlag", "PaymentFrequency"
)

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(book26[, c(predictors, "YearTrend",
                    "Exposure", "ClaimNb",
                    "ClaimAmount")]),
  !anyNA(book27[, predictors]),
  !anyNA(book28[, predictors]),
  all(book26$Exposure > 0),
  all(book26$VehValue > 0),
  all(book27$VehValue > 0),
  all(book28$VehValue > 0)
)

# 2. HISTORICAL CLAIMS TRENDS -------------------------------

trends <- book26 %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Exposure = sum(Exposure),
    Claims = sum(ClaimNb),
    ClaimCost = sum(ClaimAmount),
    Frequency = Claims / Exposure,
    Severity = ClaimCost / Claims,
    PurePremium = ClaimCost / Exposure,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(trends)

# 3. DEFINE MODEL FORMULAS ----------------------------------

# The 2027 model includes PaymentFrequency.

factors27 <- c(
  "DriverAge", "YearsLicensed", "VehAge",
  "log(VehValue)", "VehicleType", "RiskZone",
  "log1p(Density)", "AnnualKms",
  "ExcessChosen", "GaragingLocation",
  "VehicleUse", "NCDLevel", "TenureYears",
  "MultiPolicyFlag", "PaymentFrequency"
)

# PaymentFrequency is removed for 2028.

factors28 <- setdiff(
  factors27, "PaymentFrequency"
)

# Function to fit frequency and severity GLMs.

fit_models <- function(data, factors) {
  
  rhs <- paste(
    c(factors, "YearTrend"),
    collapse = " + "
  )
  
  freq_formula <- as.formula(
    paste(
      "ClaimNb ~", rhs,
      "+ offset(log(Exposure))"
    )
  )
  
  sev_formula <- as.formula(
    paste("AvgSeverity ~", rhs)
  )
  
  # Frequency: Poisson GLM
  
  freq <- glm(
    freq_formula,
    family = poisson(link = "log"),
    data = data
  )
  
  # Severity: Gamma GLM
  
  severity_data <- data %>%
    filter(ClaimNb > 0, ClaimAmount > 0) %>%
    mutate(
      AvgSeverity = ClaimAmount / ClaimNb
    )
  
  sev <- glm(
    sev_formula,
    family = Gamma(link = "log"),
    weights = ClaimNb,
    data = severity_data
  )
  
  list(freq = freq, sev = sev)
}

# 4. SPLIT DATA FOR VALIDATION ------------------------------

train <- book26 %>%
  filter(Year <= 2025)

test <- book26 %>%
  filter(Year == 2026)

# Fit models using 2023-2025.

models_train <- fit_models(
  train, factors27
)

summary(models_train$freq)
summary(models_train$sev)

# 5. PREDICTION FUNCTION ------------------------------------

predict_technical <- function(models, data, year) {
  
  newdata <- data
  
  # Annual policy exposure
  newdata$Exposure <- 1
  
  # Project to target year
  newdata$YearTrend <- year - 2026
  
  frequency <- predict(
    models$freq,
    newdata = newdata,
    type = "response"
  )
  
  severity <- predict(
    models$sev,
    newdata = newdata,
    type = "response"
  )
  
  data.frame(
    ExpectedFrequency = as.numeric(frequency),
    ExpectedSeverity = as.numeric(severity),
    TechnicalPrice = as.numeric(
      frequency * severity
    )
  )
}

# 6. VALIDATE AGAINST 2026 ---------------------------------

pred_test <- predict_technical(
  models_train, test, 2026
)

actual_claims <- sum(test$ClaimNb)

expected_claims <- sum(
  pred_test$ExpectedFrequency * test$Exposure
)

actual_cost <- sum(test$ClaimAmount)

expected_cost <- sum(
  pred_test$TechnicalPrice * test$Exposure
)

validation <- data.frame(
  Frequency_AE = actual_claims / expected_claims,
  ClaimCost_AE = actual_cost / expected_cost,
  ClaimCost_MAE = mean(
    abs(
      test$ClaimAmount -
        pred_test$TechnicalPrice * test$Exposure
    )
  )
)

print(validation)

# Check Poisson overdispersion.

dispersion <- sum(
  residuals(models_train$freq,
            type = "pearson")^2
) / df.residual(models_train$freq)

print(dispersion)

# 7. COMPARE AGAINST A SIMPLER MODEL ------------------------

simple_factors <- c(
  "DriverAge", "log(VehValue)",
  "VehicleType", "RiskZone",
  "AnnualKms", "PaymentFrequency"
)

simple_models <- fit_models(
  train, simple_factors
)

simple_pred <- predict_technical(
  simple_models, test, 2026
)

comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Full", "Simple"),
  
  Frequency_AE = c(
    validation$Frequency_AE,
    actual_claims /
      sum(simple_pred$ExpectedFrequency *
            test$Exposure)
  ),
  
  ClaimCost_AE = c(
    validation$ClaimCost_AE,
    actual_cost /
      sum(simple_pred$TechnicalPrice *
            test$Exposure)
  ),
  
  ClaimCost_MAE = c(
    validation$ClaimCost_MAE,
    mean(abs(
      test$ClaimAmount -
        simple_pred$TechnicalPrice * test$Exposure
    ))
  )
)

print(comparison)

# 8. REFIT USING ALL HISTORICAL DATA ------------------------

models27 <- fit_models(
  book26, factors27
)

models28 <- fit_models(
  book26, factors28
)

# 9. EXAMINE FREQUENCY AND SEVERITY TRENDS -------------------

freq_trend <- exp(
  coef(models27$freq)["YearTrend"]
) - 1

sev_trend <- exp(
  coef(models27$sev)["YearTrend"]
) - 1

cat("Annual frequency trend:",
    round(freq_trend * 100, 2), "%\n")

cat("Annual severity trend:",
    round(sev_trend * 100, 2), "%\n")

# 10. TECHNICAL PRICING FOR 2027 ----------------------------

pred27 <- predict_technical(
  models27, book27, 2027
)

technical27 <- cbind(
  book27, pred27
)

cat(
  "Average 2027 technical price:",
  mean(technical27$TechnicalPrice), "\n"
)

write.csv(
  technical27,
  "data/technical_2027.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# 11. TECHNICAL PRICING FOR 2028 ----------------------------

# PaymentFrequency is excluded from this model.

pred28 <- predict_technical(
  models28, book28, 2028
)

technical28 <- cbind(
  book28, pred28
)

cat(
  "Average 2028 technical price:",
  mean(technical28$TechnicalPrice), "\n"
)

write.csv(
  technical28,
  "data/technical_2028.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# 12. SAVE FITTED MODELS ------------------------------------

saveRDS(models27, "data/models27.rds")
saveRDS(models28, "data/models28.rds")

cat("Technical pricing completed.\n")
```
